```text
Hello there!🤺

I am a first-year **Ph.D. student** in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the <img src="../assets/img/uwmadison.png" class="inline-logo" alt="UW–Madison"/>[University of Wisconsin-Madison](https://www.wisc.edu/) (UW-Madison). I joined <img src="../assets/img/skylab.png" class="inline-logo" alt="Sky-Lab"/>[Sky-Lab](https://sky-lab-uw.github.io/) at UW-Madison in Fall 2025 under the guidance of Dr.[Sikai (Sky) Chen](https://sky-lab-uw.github.io/people/). On Wisconsin!<img src="../assets/img/bucky.png" class="inline-logo" alt="Bucky"/>

Before joining UW-Madison, I obtained my M.S. in Transportation Engineering at [College of Transportation](https://tjjt.tongji.edu.cn/), <img src="../assets/img/tongji.png" class="inline-logo" alt="Tongji"/>Tongji University in 2025, and my B.E. in Vehicle Engineering at [Institute of Rail Transit](https://railway.tongji.edu.cn/main.htm), Tongji University in 2022. I am very fortunate and honored to be advised by Prof. [Hechao Zhou](https://tjjt.tongji.edu.cn/info/2943/10933.htm) and Prof. [Jimin Zhang](https://railway.tongji.edu.cn/c5/e6/c4609a50662/page.htm) during my study at Tongji University. 🫶

As for now, I am working to accelerate the development of future intelligent transportation technologies. 🧐 Specifically, I focus on:

- **Autonomous driving**
- **Vision-Language-Action model**
- **Intelligent transportation systems**
```

```text
   220	let determineComputedTheme = () => {
```

```text
# Personal Page Overview for Zilin Huang

**Page Title:** Personal | Zilin Huang

**Section Structure:**
The page contains two main sections after the navigation menu:

1. **"Memories"** - A header with no visible content below it
2. **"Leadership"** - Contains an introductory statement followed by a bulleted list of leadership positions and achievements, spanning roles from 2014-2019

3. **"Hobbies"** - Subdivided into three subsections:
   - **"Chef"** - Paragraph description with six embedded images of clay pot dishes
   - **"Basketball"** - Paragraph narrative with approximately twelve embedded photos and video placeholders spanning 2014-2023
   - **"Photography"** - Paragraph description with a bulleted list and embedded links

**Layout & Formatting:**
- Uses bullet-point lists for leadership roles and photography roles
- Entries include dates (year ranges) and descriptive text inline rather than in a dedicated column
- Features numerous embedded images throughout hobbies sections
- No visible profile photo in the provided content
- Minimal visual styling details provided; appears clean and text-focused
- Footer includes copyright notice and last update date

**Visual Elements:** Images appear integrated within hobby sections; no logos or institutional graphics mentioned.
```

```text
/*******************************************************************************
 * Styles for the base elements of the theme.

// Typography — Academic Editorial: serif display + body, sans UI, mono meta.

body {
  font-family: $ff-serif;
  font-size: $fs-base;
  line-height: $lh-body;
}

code, pre, kbd, samp, tt {
  font-family: $ff-mono;
}

p, em, div, li, span, strong {
  color: var(--global-text-color);
}

h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6 {
  color: var(--global-text-color);
}

// Display: H1 + H2 go serif for editorial gravitas; H3–H6 stay sans for UI.
h1 {
  font-family: $ff-serif;
  font-size: $fs-2xl;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  line-height: $lh-tight;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}

h2 {
  font-family: $ff-serif;
  font-size: $fs-xl;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  line-height: $lh-snug;
}

h3 {
  font-family: $ff-sans;
  font-size: $fs-lg;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  line-height: $lh-heading;
}

h4 {
  font-family: $ff-sans;
  font-size: $fs-md;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  line-height: $lh-heading;
}

h5 {
  font-family: $ff-sans;
  font-size: $fs-base;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  line-height: $lh-heading;
}

h6 {
  font-family: $ff-sans;
  font-size: $fs-sm;
  font-weight: $fw-semibold;
  letter-spacing: $tracking-wide;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--mono-meta-color);
}

hr {
  border-top: 1px solid var(--global-divider-color);
}

table {
  td,
  th {
    font-size: 1rem;
    padding: 1px 1rem 1px 0;
  }

  th {
    font-weight: bold;
  }
}

a,
table.table a {
  color: var(--global-theme-color);

  &:hover {
    color: var(--global-theme-color);
    text-decoration: underline;
  }

  &:hover:after :not(.nav-item.dropdown) {

}
```

```text
     1	# AGENTS.md
     2	
     3	This file provides guidance to Codex (Codex.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4	
     5	## Repository
     6	
     7	Personal academic website for Zhengyang Wan (UW–Madison Ph.D. student), built with Jekyll on the [al-folio](https://github.com/alshedivat/al-folio) theme. Deployed to GitHub Pages from `main` via the `Deploy site` workflow.
     8	
     9	## Common commands
    10	
    11	- Local serve (recommended): `docker compose up` — runs `amirpourmand/al-folio` image, watches `_config.yml`, livereload on http://localhost:8080. Use `docker-compose-slim.yml` for the slim variant.
    12	- Local serve (native): `bundle install && bundle exec jekyll serve --livereload` (Ruby 3.3.5 per CI).
    13	- Build (CI parity): `bundle exec jekyll build` (set `JEKYLL_ENV=production` for prod). `bin/cibuild` is a one-line wrapper.
    14	- Purge unused CSS (production only): `npx purgecss -c purgecss.config.js` after build.
    15	- Format Liquid/JS/MD: `npx prettier --write .` (config: `.prettierrc`, uses `@shopify/prettier-plugin-liquid`, `printWidth: 150`).
    16	- Manual GH Pages deploy via branch swap: `bin/deploy` (interactive; force-pushes `gh-pages`). Normally unnecessary — pushing to `main` triggers `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
    17	- Refresh dynamic data locally: `pip install -r _scripts/requirements.txt && python _scripts/fetch_scholar_citations.py` and `python _scripts/fetch_github_stars.py` (the latter wants `GITHUB_TOKEN`). These run weekly via `update-scholar-citations.yml` / `update-github-stars.yml` and write to `_data/`.
    18	
    19	## Architecture
    20	
    21	Standard al-folio Jekyll layout — most "pages" are data, not code:
    22	
    23	- `_config.yml` — site-wide config (identity, socials, plugin options, navbar, search). Editing it triggers a Jekyll restart in the docker entrypoint. CI patches `giscus.repo` automatically before building.
    24	- `_pages/` — top-level routes (`about.md`, `publications.md`, `cv.md`, `news.md`, `projects.md`, `repositories.md`, `teaching.md`, etc.). Each page's behavior is mostly driven by front matter + a `_layouts/*.liquid` template.
    25	- `_layouts/` + `_includes/` — Liquid templates. `default.liquid` wraps everything; `about.liquid` renders the homepage; `bib.liquid` renders the publications list; `distill.liquid` for long-form posts. Reusable fragments (header, footer, social icons, news, selected papers, figure/audio/video shortcodes) live in `_includes/`.
    26	- `_bibliography/papers.bib` + `_data/` — the source of truth for publications, CV, coauthors, venues, and dynamically-fetched GitHub stars / Scholar citations. `jekyll-scholar` renders `papers.bib` via `bib.liquid`; `_data/cv.yml` drives the CV page; `_data/repositories.yml` drives the repo grid.
    27	- `_news/`, `_projects/`, `_posts/` — collections; each markdown file is one item with front matter (`date`, `title`, `inline`, etc.).
    28	- `_plugins/` — custom Ruby Jekyll plugins (cache-busting, BibTeX hide/expand, external posts, file-existence guard, accent stripping, Inspire-HEP citations, third-party download caching). When publication / bibliography behavior is unexpected, look here before blaming `jekyll-scholar`.
    29	- `assets/` — static assets, Sass entry points, JS, fonts, PDFs, the rendered bibliography, plotly/jupyter exports. Sass partials live in `_sass/`.
    30	- `_scripts/` + `.github/workflows/` — Python jobs that refresh `_data/*.json` weekly; their workflows trigger the `Deploy site` workflow on success via `workflow_run`, so the site always reflects the latest fetched data.
    31	- `bin/entry_point.sh` — Docker dev entrypoint; manages `Gemfile.lock` (preserves it if tracked, removes it otherwise) and restarts Jekyll on `_config.yml` changes.
    32	
    33	## Editing notes
    34	
    35	- Adding a publication: append a BibTeX entry to `_bibliography/papers.bib`. Use `selected={true}` to surface it on the homepage's selected list.
    36	- Adding a news item: drop a new `_news/announcement_N.md` with `date` front matter; the homepage news block reads the collection in date order.
    37	- Changing site identity, navbar items, social handles, or plugin options: edit `_config.yml` (a Jekyll restart is required — automatic in docker, manual otherwise).
    38	- Don't hand-edit `_data/scholar_citations.json` or `_data/github_stars.json`; they're regenerated by the weekly bots and committed by `github-actions[bot]`.
    39	- See `CUSTOMIZE.md`, `INSTALL.md`, and `FAQ.md` for upstream al-folio documentation on theming, deployment alternatives, and common gotchas.
```

```text
  <h5 style="text-align: left;">Basketball</h5>
  <p style="text-align: justify;">
    As an avid NBA fan, my first jersey was <strong>Ming Yao</strong>'s Houston Rockets uniform. During high school, I would purchase <i>Slam Dunk</i> magazine every week. <strong>LeBron</strong> has probably had the most profound impact on me. And, <strong>Kobe</strong>'s "Mamba Mentality" has deeply influenced my way of dealing with challenges. I was fortunate enough to live in Wisconsin, where Chinese basketball star <strong>Jianlian Yi</strong> played for the Milwaukee Bucks. I remember how happy I was the day he was drafted by Milwaukee. Also, Giannis Antetokounmpo's basketball journey deeply touched me—from a skinny kid to an NBA champion.
  </p>

  <p style="text-align: justify;">
    I've been injured many times in my basketball journey, such as sprained ankles and scraped knees. The most severe setback occurred in early 2024 when I suffered a lower back injury requiring surgery. For the first two weeks, I was essentially immobile, confined to bed rest. However, these challenges never diminished my passion for the game. As <strong>Iverson</strong> famously said, "What doesn't kill you makes you stronger." Basketball has not only strengthened my body but also taught me invaluable life lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and rising after every fall.
  </p>
```

## 6. `_includes/figure.liquid` and imagemagick config

**`_includes/figure.liquid`** parameters (all via `include.*`):
- `path` (required) — image path; extension is stripped/parsed to detect `.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.tiff/.gif` for webp srcset generation.
- `slot`, `class`, `width` (default `100%`), `height` (default `auto`), `min-width`/`min-height`/`max-width`/`max-height` (inline style), `alt`, `title`, `caption` (renders `<figcaption class="caption">`), `zoomable` (adds `data-zoomable` attribute), `loading` (falls back to `site.lazy_loading_images` → `loading="lazy"`), `url` (overrides computed `src`), `cache_bust` (appends cache-busting query via `bust_file_cache`), `sizes` (defaults to `95vw` when `site.imagemagick.enabled`).
- When `site.imagemagick.enabled` is true, it emits a `<source>` element with `srcset` built from `{% for i in site.imagemagick.widths %}{{ img_path }}-{{ i }}.webp {{ i }}w{% endfor %}` for `type="image/webp"`, followed by the fallback `<img>`.

**`_config.yml` imagemagick block** (around line 398‑415):
```
imagemagick:
  enabled: true
  widths:
    - 480
    - 800
    - 1400
  input_directories:
    - assets/img/
  input_formats:
    - ".jpg"
    - ".jpeg"
    - ".png"
    - ".tiff"
    - ".gif"
  output_formats:
    webp: "-quality 85"
```
`jekyll-imagemagick` is also registered in `_config.yml`'s plugin list (line 260) and in `Gemfile` (line 9). So `.webp` variants (480/800/1400px) ARE generated for images placed under `assets/img/` with the listed extensions, and `figure.liquid` will build a responsive `srcset` automatically for any placeholder research image dropped into `assets/img/` (e.g. as `.jpg`/`.png`).

## 6. `_includes/figure.liquid` and imagemagick config

**`_includes/figure.liquid`** parameters (all via `include.*`):
- `path` (required) — image path; extension is stripped/parsed to detect `.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.tiff/.gif` for webp srcset generation.
- `slot`, `class`, `width` (default `100%`), `height` (default `auto`), `min-width`/`min-height`/`max-width`/`max-height` (inline style), `alt`, `title`, `caption` (renders `&lt;figcaption class="caption"&gt;`), `zoomable` (adds `data-zoomable` attribute), `loading` (falls back to `site.lazy_loading_images` → `loading="lazy"`), `url` (overrides computed `src`), `cache_bust` (appends cache-busting query via `bust_file_cache`), `sizes` (defaults to `95vw` when `site.imagemagick.enabled`).
- When `site.imagemagick.enabled` is true, it emits a `&lt;source&gt;` element with `srcset` built from `{% for i in site.imagemagick.widths %}{{ img_path }}-{{ i }}.webp {{ i }}w{% endfor %}` for `type="image/webp"`, followed by the fallback `&lt;img&gt;`.

**`_config.yml` imagemagick block** (around line 398‑415):
```
imagemagick:
  enabled: true
  widths:
    - 480
    - 800
    - 1400
  input_directories:
    - assets/img/
  input_formats:
    - ".jpg"
    - ".jpeg"
    - ".png"
    - ".tiff"
    - ".gif"
  output_formats:
    webp: "-quality 85"
```
`jekyll-imagemagick` is also registered in `_config.yml`'s plugin list (line 260) and in `Gemfile` (line 9). So `.webp` variants (480/800/1400px) ARE generated for images placed under `assets/img/` with the listed extensions, and `figure.liquid` will build a responsive `srcset` automatically for any placeholder research image dropped into `assets/img/` (e.g. as `.jpg`/`.png`).

## 3. `_includes/news.liquid` (36 lines) + `_news/`

Full logic:

```liquid
{% if site.news != blank %}                                              L2
  {% assign news_size = site.news | size %}                              L3
  <div
    {% if include.limit and site.announcements.scrollable and news_size > 5 %}   L5
      class="news-scroll"
      style="max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;"                        L7
    {% endif %}
  >
    {% assign news = site.news | reverse %}                              L10
    {% if include.limit and site.announcements.limit %}                  L11
      {% assign news_limit = site.announcements.limit %}                 L12
    {% else %}
      {% assign news_limit = news_size %}                                L14
    {% endif %}
    <ol class="news-list">                                               L16
      {% for item in news limit: news_limit %}                           L17
```

- **How many shown:** `site.announcements.limit` = **7** (`_config.yml:204`). Total news files = 10, so 7 render today.
- **Config key controlling the limit:** `site.announcements.limit` only. `page.news` (`_pages/about.md:15`) is a boolean gate in the layout, not a count. `include.limit=true` is passed from `_layouts/about.liquid:68` and is what activates both the limit and the scroll wrapper.
- **Sort order:** `site.news | reverse`. Jekyll orders collection documents by `date` ascending, so `reverse` = newest-first. No explicit `sort` filter (unlike `_pages/news.md:10` which does `sort: "date" | reverse`).
- **Scrollable:** `site.announcements.scrollable: true` (`_config.yml:203`). **Gotcha:** the scroll wrapper condition tests `news_size > 5` — the *total* file count (10), not the rendered limit. So reducing `limit` to 4 will still emit `class="news-scroll" style="max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;"` around a 4-item list. `.news-scroll` has no SCSS rule anywhere and is not in the purgecss safelist; the styling is the inline `style` attribute.
- Markup per item: `<li class="news-row">` → `<time class="news-date" datetime=...>{{ item.date | date: '%b %d, %Y' }}</time>` + `<div class="news-body">`; if `item.inline` the raw content is emitted with `<p>` stripped and `| emojify`, else an `<a class="news-title">` to the item page.
- Styles: `_sass/_base.scss:595-661` (CSS grid, `minmax(10ch, 12ch) 1fr`, mono date + serif body, hairline row separators, collapses to 1 column ≤576px).

So the pattern is: **bare `<a href title>` wrapping a bare `<i>` — no CSS classes on the anchor at all.** All visual styling is inherited from the `.social .contact-icons a i::before` descendant selector. Icon classes are either FontAwesome (`fa-brands fa-*`, `fa-solid fa-*`) or academicons (`ai ai-*`).

**Styling** — `_sass/_base.scss:481-511`:
```scss
.social {
  text-align: left;
  .contact-icons {
    font-size: 1.6rem;
    margin-bottom: $sp-3;
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: $sp-4;
    a {
      i::before { color: var(--mono-meta-color); transition: color $dur-base $ease-out; }
      &:hover { i::before { color: var(--global-theme-color); } }
    }
  }
  .contact-note { font-family: $ff-mono; font-size: $fs-xs; color: var(--mono-meta-color); letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
}
```
Because it's a flexbox with `gap`, a new `<a><i>` inserted anywhere in `social.liquid` picks up spacing and hover color automatically. `deep: [/^ai-/, /^fa-/]` in `purgecss.config.js:53` protects any new FA/AI icon class from purging.

**Existing generic / non-username entry types in `social.liquid`:** these take a URL or a flag rather than a username, and are the closest analogues to a CV link —
- L67-69 `site.work_url` → `<a href="{{ site.work_url }}" title="Work"><i class="fa-solid fa-briefcase"></i></a>` (currently empty at `_config.yml:109`)
- L64-66 `site.blogger_url`, L85-87 `site.dblp_url`, L112-114 `site.bluesky_url` — same shape
- L124-126 `site.rss_icon` → `<a href="{{ site.baseurl }}/feed.xml" title="RSS Feed"><i class="fa-solid fa-square-rss"></i></a>` (flag-gated, `rss_icon: false` at `_config.yml:43`)
- L1-3 `site.email` → `mailto:` with `| encode_email` filter, `<i class="fa-solid fa-envelope"></i>`
- L127-133 `site.wechat_qr` → the only entry using `prepend: 'assets/img/' | relative_url`, plus a modal include. **This is the one existing example of an asset-path-based social entry**, and the pattern `{{ site.cv_pdf | prepend: 'assets/pdf/' | relative_url }}` would mirror it.

## 3. `_includes/news.liquid` (36 lines) + `_news/`

Full logic:

```liquid
{% if site.news != blank %}                                              L2
  {% assign news_size = site.news | size %}                              L3
  &lt;div
    {% if include.limit and site.announcements.scrollable and news_size &gt; 5 %}   L5
      class="news-scroll"
      style="max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;"                        L7
    {% endif %}
  &gt;
    {% assign news = site.news | reverse %}                              L10
    {% if include.limit and site.announcements.limit %}                  L11
      {% assign news_limit = site.announcements.limit %}                 L12
    {% else %}
      {% assign news_limit = news_size %}                                L14
    {% endif %}
    &lt;ol class="news-list"&gt;                                               L16
      {% for item in news limit: news_limit %}                           L17
```

- **How many shown:** `site.announcements.limit` = **7** (`_config.yml:204`). Total news files = 10, so 7 render today.
- **Config key controlling the limit:** `site.announcements.limit` only. `page.news` (`_pages/about.md:15`) is a boolean gate in the layout, not a count. `include.limit=true` is passed from `_layouts/about.liquid:68` and is what activates both the limit and the scroll wrapper.
- **Sort order:** `site.news | reverse`. Jekyll orders collection documents by `date` ascending, so `reverse` = newest-first. No explicit `sort` filter (unlike `_pages/news.md:10` which does `sort: "date" | reverse`).
- **Scrollable:** `site.announcements.scrollable: true` (`_config.yml:203`). **Gotcha:** the scroll wrapper condition tests `news_size &gt; 5` — the *total* file count (10), not the rendered limit. So reducing `limit` to 4 will still emit `class="news-scroll" style="max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;"` around a 4-item list. `.news-scroll` has no SCSS rule anywhere and is not in the purgecss safelist; the styling is the inline `style` attribute.
- Markup per item: `&lt;li class="news-row"&gt;` → `&lt;time class="news-date" datetime=...&gt;{{ item.date | date: '%b %d, %Y' }}&lt;/time&gt;` + `&lt;div class="news-body"&gt;`; if `item.inline` the raw content is emitted with `&lt;p&gt;` stripped and `| emojify`, else an `&lt;a class="news-title"&gt;` to the item page.
- Styles: `_sass/_base.scss:595-661` (CSS grid, `minmax(10ch, 12ch) 1fr`, mono date + serif body, hairline row separators, collapses to 1 column ≤576px).

## 4. Social icons

**Include:** `_includes/social.liquid` — 133 lines. **There is no `_data/socials.yml`.** `_data/` contains only: `coauthors.yml`, `cv.yml`, `github_stars.json`, `repositories.yml`, `scholar_citations.json`, `venues.yml`.

The include is a flat list of 40+ hardcoded `{% if site.&lt;key&gt; %}` blocks reading top-level `_config.yml` keys. No loop, no data file, no `custom_social` / generic-link mechanism.

**Exact markup pattern (GitHub, `_includes/social.liquid:43-45`):**
```liquid
{% if site.github_username %}
  &lt;a href="https://github.com/{{ site.github_username }}" title="GitHub"&gt;&lt;i class="fa-brands fa-github"&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
{% endif %}
```

Google Scholar (L10-12) uses academicons:
```liquid
{% if site.scholar_userid %}
  &lt;a href="https://scholar.google.com/citations?user={{ site.scholar_userid }}" title="Google Scholar"&gt;&lt;i class="ai ai-google-scholar"&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/a&gt;
{% endif %}
```

So the pattern is: **bare `&lt;a href title&gt;` wrapping a bare `&lt;i&gt;` — no CSS classes on the anchor at all.** All visual styling is inherited from the `.social .contact-icons a i::before` descendant selector. Icon classes are either FontAwesome (`fa-brands fa-*`, `fa-solid fa-*`) or academicons (`ai ai-*`).

**Styling** — `_sass/_base.scss:481-511`:
```scss
.social {
  text-align: left;
  .contact-icons {
    font-size: 1.6rem;
    margin-bottom: $sp-3;
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: $sp-4;
    a {
      i::before { color: var(--mono-meta-color); transition: color $dur-base $ease-out; }
      &amp;:hover { i::before { color: var(--global-theme-color); } }
    }
  }
  .contact-note { font-family: $ff-mono; font-size: $fs-xs; color: var(--mono-meta-color); letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
}
```
Because it's a flexbox with `gap`, a new `&lt;a&gt;&lt;i&gt;` inserted anywhere in `social.liquid` picks up spacing and hover color automatically. `deep: [/^ai-/, /^fa-/]` in `purgecss.config.js:53` protects any new FA/AI icon class from purging.

**Existing generic / non-username entry types in `social.liquid`:** these take a URL or a flag rather than a username, and are the closest analogues to a CV link —
- L67-69 `site.work_url` → `&lt;a href="{{ site.work_url }}" title="Work"&gt;&lt;i class="fa-solid fa-briefcase"&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/a&gt;` (currently empty at `_config.yml:109`)
- L64-66 `site.blogger_url`, L85-87 `site.dblp_url`, L112-114 `site.bluesky_url` — same shape

```yaml
201-204: announcements: {enabled: true, scrollable: true, limit: 7}
```

**There is no config key that forces a default theme.** The default is decided purely in JS.

## 1.2 Initial theme selection (JS)

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../_includes/head.liquid` lines 71–84 — `theme.js` is loaded **synchronously in `<head>`**, and `initTheme()` is called only when `site.enable_darkmode` is true:
```liquid
71: <!-- Dark Mode -->
72: <script src="{{ '/assets/js/theme.js' | relative_url | bust_file_cache }}"></script>
73: {% if site.enable_darkmode %}
74:   <link defer rel="stylesheet" href=".../jekyll-pygments-themes-native.css" media="none" id="highlight_theme_dark">
81:   <script>
82:     initTheme();
83:   </script>
84: {% endif %}
```

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../assets/js/theme.js` — the decision chain. **Default is `"system"`, i.e. it follows `prefers-color-scheme`. There is no hard-coded `data-theme="dark"`.**

Lines 208–216:
```js
// Determine the expected state of the theme toggle, which can be "dark", "light", or
// "system". Default is "system".
let determineThemeSetting = () => {
  let themeSetting = localStorage.getItem("theme");
  if (themeSetting != "dark" && themeSetting != "light" && themeSetting != "system") {
    themeSetting = "system";
  }
  return themeSetting;
};
```

Lines 218–232:
```js
let determineComputedTheme = () => {
  let themeSetting = determineThemeSetting();
  if (themeSetting == "system") {
    const userPref = window.matchMedia;
    if (userPref && userPref("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
      return "dark";
    } else {
      return "light";
    }
  } else {
    return themeSetting;
  }
};
```

Lines 234–252 (`initTheme`) calls `setThemeSetting(themeSetting)`, which at line 17 **writes to localStorage on every page load**: `localStorage.setItem("theme", themeSetting);` and sets `data-theme-setting`. Line 53 sets `document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", theme);`.

Lines 248–251 also re-apply on OS preference change:
```js
window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").addEventListener("change", ({ matches }) => {
  applyTheme();
});
```

**Consequence:** if the user's OS is in dark mode, the site renders dark on first visit; if they ever clicked the toggle, `localStorage.theme` pins it.

## 2.5 Spacing tokens (the knobs)

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../_sass/_tokens.scss` lines 138–147:

`$sp-8` and `$sp-9` are **declared but never used** (`grep '\$sp-8\|\$sp-9' _sass/` returns only the declarations). Every large section gap resolves to `$sp-6` (32px) or `$sp-7` (48px). Full list of `$sp-7` consumers:

## 2.6 `<br>` / empty-paragraph whitespace in content

- `_pages/about.md` — **no `<br>`**, no empty paragraphs. Front matter ends line 18; content is plain markdown paragraphs.
- `_layouts/about.liquid` — no `<br>`. Line 19 has an inline style adding margin: `<div class="social" style="text-align: left; margin-top: 0.5rem;">`. # 3. PURGECSS

**Yes, purgecss runs in production and will strip any new class not present in the built HTML or safelisted.**

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` lines 94–102:
```yaml
- name: Install and Build 🔧
  run: |
    pip3 install --upgrade nbconvert
    export JEKYLL_ENV=production
    bundle exec jekyll build
- name: Purge unused CSS 🧹
  run: |
    npm install -g purgecss
    purgecss -c purgecss.config.js
```

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../purgecss.config.js` (whole file):
```js
module.exports = {
  content: ["_site/**/*.html", "_site/**/*.js"],
  css: ["_site/assets/css/*.css"],
  output: "_site/assets/css/",
  skippedContentGlobs: ["_site/assets/**/*.html"],
  safelist: {
    standard: [
      "open", "active", "bio", "eyebrow", "meta-strip", "inline-logo",
      "section-rule", "home-section", "profile__card", "mono-meta",
      "footer__ornament", "author-self", "selected-dot", "venue",
      "stat-pill", "stat-pill-row", "stat-pill__label", "stat-pill__value",
      "badge-pill", "badge-pill__label", "badge-pill__value",
      "news-list", "news-row", "news-date", "news-body", "news-title",
      "news-year", "news-archive",
      "cv-section", "cv-section__title", "cv-timeline", "cv-year", "cv-entry",
      "cv-pdf-button", "btn-outline-accent", "cv-year-badge",
      "filter-chips", "project-tags", "project-meta", "search-pill",
      "expand-panel", "about-header", "about-title", "about-subtitle",
    ],
    deep: [/^cv-/, /^news-/, /^stat-pill/, /^badge-pill/, /^project-/, /^ti-/, /^ai-/, /^fa-/],
    greedy: [/^tabler/, /^font-awesome/],
  },
};
```

Implications:
- **Element selectors (`body`, `h1`, `article`, `hr`, `footer`) and `:root` / `html[data-theme=...]` are never purged** — purgecss only removes selectors whose *class/id* tokens are absent. So changing `--global-bg-color` in `_themes.scss` or tweaking existing margins is purgecss-safe.
- **Any brand-new class name must appear in the generated HTML**, otherwise it must be added to the `standard` safelist. Note the existing precedent: `about-header`, `about-title`, `about-subtitle` are safelisted (and used in `_layouts/about.liquid:5-6,15`) but **have zero CSS rules anywhere in `_sass/`** — verified by repo-wide grep; the only other hits are in `.specstory/history/*.md` transcripts. They are free hooks.
- The `deep` regexes mean any new class starting `cv-`, `news-`, `stat-pill`, `badge-pill`, or `project-` is automatically kept.
- The trigger paths for `deploy.yml` include `"assets/**"` and `"**.md"` but **not `_sass/**`** — editing only `_sass/*.scss` will **not** trigger the deploy workflow on push (the `.scss` extension is not in the paths list, and `_sass` is outside `assets/`). Touching `assets/css/main.scss` (matches `assets/**`) or any `.liquid`/`.md`/`.yml` file would trigger it.

## 1.2 Initial theme selection (JS)

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../_includes/head.liquid` lines 71–84 — `theme.js` is loaded **synchronously in `&lt;head&gt;`**, and `initTheme()` is called only when `site.enable_darkmode` is true:
```liquid

73: {% if site.enable_darkmode %}

81:   &lt;script&gt;
82:     initTheme();
83:   &lt;/script&gt;
84: {% endif %}
```

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../assets/js/theme.js` — the decision chain. **Default is `"system"`, i.e. it follows `prefers-color-scheme`. There is no hard-coded `data-theme="dark"`.**

Lines 208–216:
```js
// Determine the expected state of the theme toggle, which can be "dark", "light", or
// "system". Default is "system".
let determineThemeSetting = () =&gt; {
  let themeSetting = localStorage.getItem("theme");
  if (themeSetting != "dark" &amp;&amp; themeSetting != "light" &amp;&amp; themeSetting != "system") {
    themeSetting = "system";
  }
  return themeSetting;
};
```

Lines 218–232:
```js
let determineComputedTheme = () =&gt; {
  let themeSetting = determineThemeSetting();
  if (themeSetting == "system") {
    const userPref = window.matchMedia;
    if (userPref &amp;&amp; userPref("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
      return "dark";
    } else {
      return "light";
    }
  } else {
    return themeSetting;
  }
};
```

Lines 234–252 (`initTheme`) calls `setThemeSetting(themeSetting)`, which at line 17 **writes to localStorage on every page load**: `localStorage.setItem("theme", themeSetting);` and sets `data-theme-setting`. Line 53 sets `document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", theme);`.

Lines 248–251 also re-apply on OS preference change:
```js
window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").addEventListener("change", ({ matches }) =&gt; {
  applyTheme();
});
```

**Consequence:** if the user's OS is in dark mode, the site renders dark on first visit; if they ever clicked the toggle, `localStorage.theme` pins it.

# 3. PURGECSS

**Yes, purgecss runs in production and will strip any new class not present in the built HTML or safelisted.**

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` lines 94–102:
```yaml
- name: Install and Build 🔧
  run: |
    pip3 install --upgrade nbconvert
    export JEKYLL_ENV=production
    bundle exec jekyll build
- name: Purge unused CSS 🧹
  run: |
    npm install -g purgecss
    purgecss -c purgecss.config.js
```

`/Users/jamesyoung/.../purgecss.config.js` (whole file):
```js
module.exports = {
  content: ["_site/**/*.html", "_site/**/*.js"],
  css: ["_site/assets/css/*.css"],
  output: "_site/assets/css/",
  skippedContentGlobs: ["_site/assets/**/*.html"],
  safelist: {
    standard: [
      "open", "active", "bio", "eyebrow", "meta-strip", "inline-logo",
      "section-rule", "home-section", "profile__card", "mono-meta",
      "footer__ornament", "author-self", "selected-dot", "venue",
      "stat-pill", "stat-pill-row", "stat-pill__label", "stat-pill__value",

      "cv-section", "cv-section__title", "cv-timeline", "cv-year", "cv-entry",

    deep: [/^cv-/, /^news-/, /^stat-pill/, /^badge-pill/, /^project-/, /^ti-/, /^ai-/, /^fa-/],

```

Implications:
- **Element selectors (`body`, `h1`, `article`, `hr`, `footer`) and `:root` / `html[data-theme=...]` are never purged** — purgecss only removes selectors whose *class/id* tokens are absent. So changing `--global-bg-color` in `_themes.scss` or tweaking existing margins is purgecss-safe.
- **Any brand-new class name must appear in the generated HTML**, otherwise it must be added to the `standard` safelist. Note the existing precedent: `about-header`, `about-title`, `about-subtitle` are safelisted (and used in `_layouts/about.liquid:5-6,15`) but **have zero CSS rules anywhere in `_sass/`** — verified by repo-wide grep; the only other hits are in `.specstory/history/*.md` transcripts. They are free hooks.
- The `deep` regexes mean any new class starting `cv-`, `news-`, `stat-pill`, `badge-pill`, or `project-` is automatically kept.
- The trigger paths for `deploy.yml` include `"assets/**"` and `"**.md"` but **not `_sass/**`** — editing only `_sass/*.scss` will **not** trigger the deploy workflow on push (the `.scss` extension is not in the paths list, and `_sass` is outside `assets/`). :root {
```text
  // Surfaces (Claude cream — warmer than prior warm off-white)
  --global-bg-color:           #{$cream-bg};
  --global-card-bg-color:      #{$n-0};

html[data-theme="dark"] {

  --global-divider-color:      #{$hairline-warm-dark};

  --global-back-to-top-bg-color: rgba(

  .repo-img-light { display: none; }
  .repo-img-dark  { display: block; }
}

html[data-theme-setting="dark"] {
  #light-toggle-system { display: none; }
  #light-toggle-dark {
```

```text
          python-version: "3.13"

      - name: Update _config.yml ⚙️
        uses: fjogeleit/yaml-update-action@main
        with:
          commitChange: false
          valueFile: "_config.yml"
          propertyPath: "giscus.repo"
          value: ${{ github.repository }}
      - name: Install and Build 🔧
        run: |
          pip3 install --upgrade nbconvert
          export JEKYLL_ENV=production
          bundle exec jekyll build
      - name: Purge unused CSS 🧹
        run: |
          npm install -g purgecss
          purgecss -c purgecss.config.js
      - name: Deploy 🚀
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4
        with:
          folder: _site
```

```text
// Has to be in the head tag, otherwise a flicker effect will occur.

// Toggle through light, dark, and system theme settings.
let toggleThemeSetting = () => {
  let themeSetting = determineThemeSetting();
  if (themeSetting == "system") {
    setThemeSetting("light");
  } else if (themeSetting == "light") {
    setThemeSetting("dark");
  } else {
    setThemeSetting("system");
  }
};

// Change the theme setting and apply the theme.
let setThemeSetting = (themeSetting) => {
  localStorage.setItem("theme", themeSetting);

  document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme-setting", themeSetting);

  applyTheme();
};

// Apply the computed dark or light theme to the website.
let applyTheme = () => {
  let theme = determineComputedTheme();

  transTheme();
  setHighlight(theme);
  setGiscusTheme(theme);
  setSearchTheme(theme);

  // if mermaid is not defined, do nothing
  if (typeof mermaid !== "undefined") {
    setMermaidTheme(theme);
  }

  // if diff2html is not defined, do nothing
  if (typeof Diff2HtmlUI !== "undefined") {
    setDiff2htmlTheme(theme);
=====200-260
    ninjaKeys.classList.add("dark");
  } else {
    ninjaKeys.classList.remove("dark");
  }
};

let transTheme = () => {
  document.documentElement.classList.add("transition");
  window.setTimeout(() => {
    document.documentElement.classList.remove("transition");
  }, 500);
};

// Determine the expected state of the theme toggle, which can be "dark", "light", or
// "system". Default is "system".
let determineThemeSetting = () => {
  let themeSetting = localStorage.getItem("theme");
  if (themeSetting != "dark" && themeSetting != "light" && themeSetting != "system") {
    themeSetting = "system";
  }
  return themeSetting;
};

// Determine the computed theme, which can be "dark" or "light". If the theme setting is
// "system", the computed theme is determined based on the user's system preference.
let determineComputedTheme = () => {
  let themeSetting = determineThemeSetting();
  if (themeSetting == "system") {
    const userPref = window.matchMedia;
    if (userPref && userPref("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
      return "dark";
    } else {
      return "light";
    }
  } else {
    return themeSetting;
  }
};

let initTheme = () => {
  let themeSetting = determineThemeSetting();

  setThemeSetting(themeSetting);

  // Add event listener to the theme toggle button.
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    const mode_toggle = document.getElementById("light-toggle");

    mode_toggle.addEventListener("click", function () {
      toggleThemeSetting();
    });
  });

  // Add event listener to the system theme preference change.
  window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").addEventListener("change", ({ matches }) => {
    applyTheme();
  });
};
```

```text
/*******************************************************************************
 * CV — Academic Editorial timeline.
 *
 * Sections render as <section class="cv-section"> with a serif title and a
 * hairline rule. Time-table entries use a CSS grid with a year gutter
 * on the left, institution/role/items on the right.
 ******************************************************************************/

.cv {
  font-family: $ff-serif;
}

// ------------ CV page header + PDF button ---------------------------------
.cv-pdf-button {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  right: 0;

  i { margin-right: $sp-1; }
}

@media (max-width: 576px) {
  .cv-pdf-button {
    position: static;
    margin-top: $sp-3;
  }
}

// ------------ Section wrapper ---------------------------------------------
.cv-section {
  font-family: $ff-serif;
  margin-top: $sp-7;
  margin-bottom: $sp-5;

  &:first-child { margin-top: $sp-5; }

  .cv-section__title {
    font-family: $ff-serif;
    font-size: $fs-xl;
    font-weight: $fw-semibold;
    color: var(--global-text-color);
    margin: 0 0 $sp-4;
    padding-bottom: $sp-3;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline);
    letter-spacing: -0.005em;
  }
}

// ------------ Anchor (offset so #id scrolls below the fixed nav) ---------
a.anchor {
  display: block;
  position: relative;
  top: -50px;
  visibility: hidden;
}

// ------------ Time-table entries ------------------------------------------
// Structure emitted by _includes/cv/time_table.liquid:
//   <ul.card-text.font-weight-light.list-group.list-group-flush>
```

```bash
function lin(c){c/=255;return c<=0.03928?c/12.92:Math.pow((c+0.055)/1.055,2.4);}
function L(hex){const r=parseInt(hex.slice(1,3),16),g=parseInt(hex.slice(3,5),16),b=parseInt(hex.slice(5,7),16);return 0.2126*lin(r)+0.7152*lin(g)+0.0722*lin(b);}
function C(a,b){const l1=L(a),l2=L(b);const hi=Math.max(l1,l2),lo=Math.min(l1,l2);return ((hi+0.05)/(lo+0.05)).toFixed(2);}
const pairs=[["#B3654A","#F0EEE6"],["#B3654A","#FFFFFF"],["#8C4A32","#FFFFFF"],["#141413","#FFFFFF"],["#6B6B6A","#FFFFFF"],["#6B6B6A","#F0EEE6"],["#141413","#F3F4F6"],["#FFFFFF","#141413"],["#CC785C","#FFFFFF"]];
for(const [f,b] of pairs) console.log(f,"on",b,"=",C(f,b));
'
```

## C. Homepage news limit → 4

`_config.yml` **L203-204**:

```yaml
announcements:
  enabled: true
  scrollable: false # no scroll wrapper — the homepage shows a fixed short list
  limit: 4 # leave blank to include all the news in the `_news` folder
```

**Why `scrollable: false` is sufficient:** `_includes/news.liquid:5` gates the wrapper on `include.limit and site.announcements.scrollable and news_size > 5`, where `news_size = site.news | size` = **10** (count of files in `_news/`), *not* the limit. Setting `limit: 4` alone leaves `10 > 5` true and keeps the `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` div. Flipping `scrollable` to `false` short-circuits the condition; the div then renders with no attributes, which is inert. `_pages/news.md` has its own markup and is unaffected; `latest_posts.scrollable` is a separate key.

## A. Theme → pure white, default `light`

### A1. `_sass/_tokens.scss` — 3 value edits (keep the names; do NOT rename)

Renaming `$cream-*` would touch 12 lines in `_themes.scss` for zero visual gain. Change values only and fix the comments.

**L26-27** (currently `$cream-bg: #F0EEE6;` / `$cream-subtle: #E8E4D8;`):

```scss
// Light neutrals (formerly Claude cream — now pure white surfaces)
$cream-bg:           #FFFFFF !default;   // was #F0EEE6
$cream-subtle:       #F3F4F6 !default;   // was #E8E4D8 (== $n-100)
```

**L36** (`$hairline-cream: rgba(20, 20, 19, 0.10) !default;`):

```scss
$hairline-cream:     rgba(20, 20, 19, 0.12) !default;  // was 0.10 — slightly denser so it reads on pure white
```

`$cream-subtle` **must not** become white: it backs `--global-bg-subtle` / `--global-code-bg-color`, consumed at `_sass/_base.scss:938` (`.project-tags li`), `:1072` (`.stat-pill__label`), `:1332` (`.badge-pill__label`), `:1401` / `:1416` (`pre`, `code`), `_sass/_distill.scss:58`. `$n-100 #f3f4f6` already exists in the token file (L86) — reusing its value keeps the palette honest.

Also update the block comment at **L25** (`// Claude warm neutrals`) and the file header at **L9-12** if desired — cosmetic only.

### A2. `_sass/_themes.scss` — comment-only (optional)

No rule changes needed. Every light-mode surface already flows through `$cream-bg` / `$cream-subtle`. Optionally reword the header comment (L1-9) from "Light surfaces use Claude cream #F0EEE6" → "Light surfaces are pure white #FFFFFF". `--global-hover-text-color`, `--global-back-to-top-text-color`, `--global-newsletter-bg-color` all resolve to `$cream-bg` → white, which is correct in all three cases (text on rust background, text on the translucent-black back-to-top circle, newsletter panel).

### A3. `assets/js/theme.js` — exactly one line

**L213**, inside `determineThemeSetting()`:

```js
    themeSetting = "light";
```

(was `themeSetting = "system";`)

**Confirmed nothing else assumes `"system"`:**
- `toggleThemeSetting()` (L4-13) cycles `system → light → dark → system`. With a `light` default the first click gives dark, the second gives system, the third light. The cycle still works and `system` stays reachable. *Optional* 2-state simplification (flagged, not required): replace L6-12 with `if (themeSetting == "dark") { setThemeSetting("light"); } else { setThemeSetting("dark"); }`.
- `initTheme()` (L234) always calls `setThemeSetting(...)`, which sets `data-theme-setting` on `&lt;html&gt;` synchronously in `&lt;head&gt;` (`_includes/head.liquid:81-83`). So the `:root` fallback in `_sass/_themes.scss:70-75` (which shows `#light-toggle-system`) never survives past init, and the `html[data-theme-setting="light"]` block at L165-173 correctly shows `#light-toggle-light`. No icon change needed.
- The `prefers-color-scheme` listener at L249-251 stays; it only re-applies when the setting is `system`.

### A4. Grep results — no other hardcoded warm values

`grep -rn "cream|#F0EEE6|#E8E4D8|warm-dark" _sass/ _includes/ _layouts/ assets/css/` returns only icon-font entries (`ti-ice-cream`, `fa-var-ice-cream`) and one unlinked `jupyter-grade3.css` value. Everything visual is CSS-var driven.

### A5. Cards on white — no action needed

`.card` at `_sass/_base.scss:218` sets only `background-color: var(--global-card-bg-color)` (= `$n-0` = white, i.e. equal to the page background), but Bootstrap 4.6.2's base `.card` supplies `border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.125); border-radius: .25rem`, **and** the projects page overrides it at `_sass/_base.scss:869-874` with an explicit `border: 1px solid var(--hairline); border-radius: $r-md`. Project cards therefore stay visible on white. `.code-display-wrapper .copy` (L1496) sits on top of code blocks, which keep `$cream-subtle` grey.

### A6. Contrast (computed, for the record)

| pair | on cream `#F0EEE6` | on white `#FFFFFF` |
|---|---|---|
| accent `$rust-600 #B3654A` | 3.71:1 | **4.31:1** |
| body `$claude-ink #141413` | 15.7:1 | **18.43:1** |
| meta `$claude-ink-light #6B6B6A` | 4.59:1 | **5.33:1** |

Every value improves. The accent still sits just under AA 4.5:1 for normal text. **Optional one-line fix** (flag to the user, not part of the required change): `_sass/_themes.scss:29` `--global-theme-color: #{$rust-700};` → 6.69:1, at the cost of a visibly darker rust.

### A7. Returning-visitor caveat

`assets/js/theme.js:17` writes `localStorage.theme` on every load, so anyone who has already visited the site keeps their stored `"system"` / `"dark"` value and will not see the new `light` default until they clear site data or cycle the toggle back to light.

## B. Spacing — targeted per-rule edits (NOT a token rescale)

**Decision: option (ii), targeted.** `grep -rn '\$sp-6|\$sp-7|\$sp-8|\$sp-9' _sass/*.scss` returns only **13 consumers** across three files. Rescaling `$sp-6`/`$sp-7` would silently change `.header-bar` padding, `footer.sticky-bottom` padding and the sticky offset along with the section margins, and would leave the scale name/value contract broken for future work. Editing 13 lines is smaller *and* safer.

### B1. `_layouts/default.liquid` — L24

```liquid
    &lt;div class="container mt-4" role="main"&gt;
```

Bootstrap 4.6.2: `.mt-5 = 3rem = 48px` → `.mt-4 = 1.5rem = 24px`. Combined with `body.fixed-top-nav { padding-top: 56px }` (`_sass/_layout.scss:16`), the gap above every page H1 goes **104px → 80px**.

| 132 | `margin-top: $sp-6;` | `margin-top: $sp-4;` |
| 143 | `margin: $sp-2 0 $sp-5;` | `margin: 0 0 $sp-4;` |
| 166 | `margin-top: $sp-7;` | `margin-top: $sp-6;` |
| 167 | `padding-top: $sp-5;` | `padding-top: $sp-4;` |

| 730 | `padding-bottom: $sp-4;` | `padding-bottom: $sp-3;` | 16 → 12 → **~24px below every page header rule** |
| 862 | `margin-top: $sp-5;` | `margin-top: $sp-4;` | `.projects`: 24 → 16 |
| 989 | `margin: $sp-5 0 $sp-5;` | `margin: $sp-4 0 $sp-4;` | `.filter-chips` — **dead CSS** (no markup emits it; grep of `_pages/`, `_includes/`, `_layouts/`, `assets/js/` finds nothing). Change is cosmetic; safe to skip. |
| 990 | `padding-bottom: $sp-3;` | `padding-bottom: $sp-2;` | as above |
| 1032 | `margin-top: $sp-5;` | `margin-top: $sp-4;` | `.publications`: 24 → 16 (also affects the homepage `selected_papers.liquid` wrapper) |
| 1040 | `margin: $sp-6 0 $sp-4;` | *(leave)* | `.publications h1` — no h1 is ever emitted inside `.publications`; dead |
| 1049 | `margin: $sp-4 0 $sp-5;` | `margin: $sp-3 0 $sp-4;` | `.stat-pill-row`: 16/24 → 12/16 |
| 1100 | `padding-top: $sp-4;` | `padding-top: $sp-3;` | `h2.bibliography`: 16 → 12 |

| 1107 | `top: $sp-7;` | `top: 56px; // navbar height (see body.fixed-top-nav in _layout.scss)` | **decouple from the token** — the navbar is 56px tall, so the current 48px lets the sticky year header slide 8px under it |
| 1120 | `padding: $sp-5 0;` | `padding: $sp-4 0;` | `ol.bibliography &gt; li`: 24 → 16 |

**Not changed:** `.post-description { margin-bottom: 2rem }` (L279) is overridden by `.post-header .post-description { margin: 0 }` (L747) and applies nowhere else. `.news-list .news-row { padding: $sp-3 0 }` (L604) is already tight. `_sass/_cv.scss` `.cv-section` (L30-35) becomes dead — leave it.

## C. Homepage news limit → 4

`_config.yml` **L203-204**:

```yaml
announcements:
  enabled: true
  scrollable: false # no scroll wrapper — the homepage shows a fixed short list
  limit: 4 # leave blank to include all the news in the `_news` folder
```

**Why `scrollable: false` is sufficient:** `_includes/news.liquid:5` gates the wrapper on `include.limit and site.announcements.scrollable and news_size &gt; 5`, where `news_size = site.news | size` = **10** (count of files in `_news/`), *not* the limit. Setting `limit: 4` alone leaves `10 &gt; 5` true and keeps the `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` div. Flipping `scrollable` to `false` short-circuits the condition; the div then renders with no attributes, which is inert. `_pages/news.md` has its own markup and is unaffected; `latest_posts.scrollable` is a separate key.

## F. `/cv/` → `/about-me/`

### F1. Delete `_pages/cv.md`

Repo-wide grep for links to `/cv/` returns **nothing** outside `_pages/cv.md` itself. `_layouts/cv.liquid`, `_data/cv.yml`, `_sass/_cv.scss`, `_includes/cv/`, `_includes/resume/` all stay in place, unused and harmless (they carry no top-level side effects).

### F2. New file `_pages/about-me.md` — full contents

**Body format decision: raw HTML, not markdown.** All three existing content pages in this repo (`_pages/publications.md`, `_pages/projects.md`, `_pages/news.md`) already use raw HTML blocks inside a `.md` file. `markdown="1"` on a wrapper div would work under kramdown+GFM but adds a subtle failure mode around the `{% include figure.liquid %}` output. Raw HTML matches the house pattern and makes the "copy this block" instructions unambiguous.

```markdown
---
layout: page
permalink: /about-me/
title: About me
description: &lt;i&gt;A few things beyond the papers.&lt;/i&gt;
nav: true
nav_order: 5
---

&lt;div class="about-me"&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;
    Placeholder intro paragraph — replace this with a couple of sentences about
    yourself outside of research.
  &lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!-- =====================================================================
       HOW TO ADD A NEW SECTION
       Copy an &lt;h4&gt;Title&lt;/h4&gt; line and put your content under it.
       The short accent bar under the heading is drawn automatically by CSS.
       ===================================================================== --&gt;

  &lt;h4&gt;Hobbies&lt;/h4&gt;

  &lt;p&gt;Placeholder — one or two sentences about your hobbies.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;!-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
       HOW TO ADD A PHOTO ROW
       Copy the whole &lt;div class="row photo-row"&gt; block. Each photo is one
       &lt;div class="col-md-4"&gt;, three per row. Drop your image into
       assets/img/ and change path="assets/img/YOURFILE.jpg".
       Delete the &lt;p class="photo-caption"&gt; line if you do not want a caption.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------- --&gt;
  &lt;div class="row photo-row"&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/1.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/2.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/3.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;
  &lt;p class="photo-caption"&gt;Placeholder caption — replace or delete this line.&lt;/p&gt;

  &lt;h4&gt;Travel&lt;/h4&gt;

  &lt;!-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
       HOW TO ADD A BULLET
       Copy one &lt;li&gt;. The &lt;span class="memory-date"&gt; is optional — delete it
       if the entry has no date.
       --------------------------------------------------------------------- --&gt;
  &lt;ul class="memories-list"&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Placeholder trip or city &lt;span class="memory-date"&gt;(2025.09–2025.12)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Placeholder trip or city &lt;span class="memory-date"&gt;(2024.06)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
    &lt;li&gt;Placeholder trip or city&lt;/li&gt;
  &lt;/ul&gt;

  &lt;div class="row photo-row"&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/4.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/5.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
    &lt;div class="col-md-4 mt-3"&gt;
      {% include figure.liquid path="assets/img/6.jpg" class="img-fluid rounded z-depth-1" alt="Placeholder photo" %}
    &lt;/div&gt;
  &lt;/div&gt;
  &lt;p class="photo-caption"&gt;Placeholder caption — replace or delete this line.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/div&gt;
```

Notes:
- **H1 kept.** `_layouts/page.liquid:13` always emits `&lt;h1 class="post-title"&gt;`. The reference site has no H1, but suppressing it would mean editing the shared layout. Keeping it matches Publications/Projects and is a deliberate deviation.
- **`description` provided**, so the unconditional `&lt;p class="post-description"&gt;` at `_layouts/page.liquid:14` has content. Even empty it would be harmless — `.post-header .post-description { margin: 0 }` (`_sass/_base.scss:747`) collapses it to zero height.
- **Headings: `h4` with a 48×3px accent bar**, mirroring the reference but built from site tokens (`$ff-serif`, `var(--global-theme-color)`) rather than the reference's raw values. `h5` available for sub-headings.
- `lazy_loading_images: true` (`_config.yml:423`) means `figure.liquid` adds `loading="lazy"` automatically — no need to pass it.
- `z-depth-1` comes from the **CDN** MDB stylesheet (`_includes/head.liquid:6-11` uses `site.third_party_libraries.mdb.url.css`; the local `assets/css/mdb.min.css` is not linked), so purgecss cannot strip it. `img-fluid`, `rounded`, `row`, `col-md-4`, `mt-3` come from the local, purged `bootstrap.min.css` but appear verbatim in the built HTML, so purgecss keeps them.

Specificity check: `.about-me h4` (0,1,1) beats the global `h4` (0,0,1) at `_sass/_base.scss:48`. `.about-me .photo-row img` (0,2,1) beats Bootstrap's `.img-fluid { height: auto }` (0,1,0) *and* the `height="auto"` presentation attribute emitted by `figure.liquid:45`, so `height: 220px; object-fit: cover` wins regardless of stylesheet order.

## H. Optional — `_sass/**` in the deploy trigger *(flag to user; not required)*

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` has **two** `paths:` lists (push at L7-31 and pull_request at L36-…). Neither includes `_sass/**`; `assets/**` covers `assets/css/main.scss` but not the partials. Every work package below also touches a `.md`, `.yml` or `.liquid` file, so a combined push *will* deploy — but a future SCSS-only commit would silently not. One line in each list:

```yaml
      - "_sass/**"
```

## I. Verification

**Environment facts:** system Ruby is `2.6.10` at `/usr/bin/ruby` (too old for modern Jekyll); Homebrew 6.0.2 is installed but has **no** ruby formula installed; `docker` absent; `convert`/`magick` (ImageMagick) **absent**; Node `v26.0.0` + `npx` present; `package.json` has only prettier dev-deps.

### Path 1 — full local Jekyll build (preferred; ~10-15 min of installs)

```
brew install ruby imagemagick
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin:$PATH"
bundle install
bundle exec jekyll serve --livereload
```

ImageMagick is required because `_config.yml:400` sets `imagemagick.enabled: true`; without it the responsive-webp generation for `drivingsimulator.jpg` / `1-6.jpg` will fail or be skipped.

Then check, page by page:

| page | checks |
|---|---|
| `/` | Background is `#ffffff` everywhere (inspect `body` computed style). Toggle icon shows the **sun** (`#light-toggle-light`) on a fresh profile / after `localStorage.removeItem('theme')`. One click → dark; warm-dark palette intact. Exactly **4** news rows, and the wrapper `&lt;div&gt;` around `.news-list` has **no** `class="news-scroll"` / no `max-height` inline style. Section order: bio → Recent News → Selected Publications → Education → Service. Education shows 3 rows with `uwmadison.png` / `tongji.png` / `tongji.png` inline logos at ~1em and grey mono periods. Service shows the single TRB line. Gap above the H1 ≈ 80px; gap between each `hr.section-rule` and the following heading ≈ 41px. Social row: envelope, **CV (ai-cv)**, then Scholar/GitHub/etc.; CV icon is the same grey→rust hover as its neighbours and opens `/assets/pdf/My_CV2505_RenderCV_sb2nov_Theme.pdf` in a new tab. |
| navbar | Order is About / Publications / Projects / **About me**. No "CV" entry. |
| `/cv/` | Returns 404. |
| `/about-me/` | Renders. `h4` headings each carry a 48×3px rust bar. Photo rows are 3-up on desktop, images all exactly 220px tall and cropped (`object-fit: cover`), stacked full-width below 768px. `.memory-date` is small grey mono. `_site/assets/img/1-480.webp` etc. exist. |
| `/publications/` | "Research" heading centred; image left ~42% and text right, vertically centred (`align-items-center`); two bold labels each over a disc bullet list; hairline below the block; then the search input. Year headers stick **below** the 56px navbar when scrolling (not tucked under it). Paper rows visibly tighter. |
| `/projects/` | Project cards still have a visible hairline border on the white background; hover lift + rust border still work. |
| `/news/` | Year headers tighter; grid unchanged. |
| responsive | Resize to ≤576px: news rows collapse to one column, `.cv-pdf-button` rule is now dead, `col-md-*` stacks, social row wraps. |
| dark mode | Cycle the toggle through dark and back; confirm no white-on-white or cream residue anywhere, especially `.stat-pill__label`, `.badge-pill__label`, `pre`/`code`. |

### Path 2 — Node-only static checks (if the Ruby install is not worth it)

1. **SCSS compiles** (writes only to stdout, no files):
   ```
   printf '$max-content-width: 1080px;\n@import "variables","tokens","themes","layout","base";\n' \
     | npx --yes sass@1 --stdin --load-path=_sass --no-source-map --style=expanded | tail -20
   ```
   `assets/css/main.scss` injects exactly one Liquid value (`$max-content-width`, L7), so this stub is complete. Skip the font-awesome/tabler imports — they are untouched and huge.
2. **Grep the compiled output** for the intended values, e.g. `| grep -E '--global-bg-color|--global-bg-subtle|\.home-list|\.about-me|\.research-interests'` and confirm `#ffffff` / `#f3f4f6`.
3. **Liquid syntax**: run `npx prettier --check "_layouts/about.liquid" "_includes/social.liquid" "_pages/*.md"` — the repo already depends on `@shopify/prettier-plugin-liquid@1.4.0`, so unbalanced `{% if %}`/`{% endif %}` will surface. (There is a `prettier.yml` workflow, so keeping the formatting clean also avoids CI noise.)
4. **YAML front matter**: `node -e "..."` or `npx --yes js-yaml _pages/about.md` on the extracted front matter to confirm the `education:`/`service:` lists parse (watch the en-dashes in the `period` values — they are safe mid-string plain scalars).
5. Then **push and verify on GitHub Pages**, watching the "Deploy site" run. Because the commit touches `.md`/`.yml`/`.liquid` files, the existing `paths:` filters will fire even without §H.
6. **purgecss sanity after deploy**: view-source the live `/about-me/` and `/publications/` and confirm `.about-me`, `.photo-row`, `.research-interests` rules survive in `assets/css/main.css` (this is the only class-name risk in the whole change set, and the safelist entries in §D4/§F4/§G3 are the insurance).

---

## J. Work split — 4 parallel packages, disjoint file sets

Split by **file ownership**, not by feature, so no two agents ever open the same file.

### WP-1 — Styling (Opus)
**Owns:** `_sass/_tokens.scss`, `_sass/_themes.scss`, `_sass/_base.scss`, `_sass/_layout.scss`, `assets/js/theme.js`, `_layouts/default.liquid`
**Does:** §A1-A3 (white tokens + `light` default), §B1-B3 (all spacing edits), §D3 (`.home-list`), §F3 (`.about-me` block), §G2 (`.research-interests` block).
Largest package; needs no output from the others because every class name it styles is fixed by this plan.

### WP-2 — Config, includes, CI (Sonnet)
**Owns:** `_config.yml`, `_includes/social.liquid`, `purgecss.config.js`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
**Does:** §C (`limit: 4`, `scrollable: false`), §E1-E2 (`cv_pdf` key + social icon), §D4 + §F4 + §G3 (**all** purgecss safelist additions in one edit: `"home-list"`, `"about-me"`, `"memories-list"`, `"memory-date"`, `"photo-row"`, `"photo-caption"`, and `/^research-interests/` in `deep`), §H if the user approves.

### WP-3 — Homepage content (Sonnet)
**Owns:** `_pages/about.md`, `_layouts/about.liquid`
**Does:** §D1 (front-matter `education:`/`service:`), §D2 (the two Liquid blocks after L81).

### WP-4 — Page content (Opus)
**Owns:** `_pages/about-me.md` (new), `_pages/cv.md` (delete), `_pages/publications.md`
**Does:** §F1-F2 (delete CV page, create About me skeleton), §G1 (research block insert).

**Shared-file resolution:**
- `purgecss.config.js` is needed by WP-1's classes but the entries are known up-front → assigned **solely to WP-2**.
- `_config.yml` is touched by both §C and §E → both assigned to **WP-2** (they are ~90 lines apart: L203-204 and L76).
- `_sass/_layout.scss` is touched by §B, §D3 and §F3 → all three assigned to **WP-1** (regions: L128-167 edits, insert after L162, append after L183).
- `_sass/_base.scss` is touched by §B and §G2 → both assigned to **WP-1**.
- No other file appears in more than one package.

**Merge order is irrelevant** (fully disjoint), but run the §I verification only after all four land — the white theme, the new classes and the safelist entries only make sense together.

```text
  }
  return themeSetting;
};
```

```text
    const userPref = window.matchMedia;
    if (userPref && userPref("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
```

```bash
def lum(h):
    h=h.lstrip('#'); c=[int(h[i:i+2],16)/255 for i in (0,2,4)]
    c=[(x/12.92 if x<=0.03928 else ((x+0.055)/1.055)**2.4) for x in c]
    return 0.2126*c[0]+0.7152*c[1]+0.0722*c[2]
def cr(a,b):
    la,lb=lum(a),lum(b); hi,lo=max(la,lb),min(la,lb); return (hi+0.05)/(lo+0.05)
print('B3654A on FFFFFF', round(cr('#B3654A','#FFFFFF'),2))
print('B3654A on F0EEE6', round(cr('#B3654A','#F0EEE6'),2))
"
```

## 需要你留意的几点

1. **我只做了静态/HTML 层面的核对，没有截图看视觉效果**——请自己打开首页、`/publications/`、`/about-me/` 看一眼间距是否合适、研究块的占位图裁剪是否好看。间距若还想再紧/再松，改 `_sass/_layout.scss` 的 `.section-rule` 和 `_sass/_base.scss` 的 `.post-header` 就够了。
2. **老访客的主题**：`theme.js` 每次加载都会写 `localStorage.theme`，你自己的浏览器如果之前存了 `system`/`dark`，需要点一次切换按钮（或清站点数据）才会变成浅色；新访客默认浅色。
3. **强调色对比度**：铁锈色 `#B3654A` 在纯白上是 4.31:1，正文小字略低于 AA 的 4.5:1（米色底上原本也只有 3.71:1）。想达标的话把 `_sass/_themes.scss` 的 `--global-theme-color` 换成 `$rust-700` 即可，颜色会明显更深，我没有擅自改。
4. **About me 内容**待你填；占位图用的是模板自带的 `assets/img/1–6.jpg`。研究块占位图也可随时换成别的 `assets/img/` 文件。
5. `_layouts/cv.liquid`、`_data/cv.yml`、`_sass/_cv.scss`、`_includes/cv/` 保留未动（现在无页面使用），随时可删。
6. `.specstory/` 下的会话文件没有提交。
